one_liner: tinyBLAS: register-tiled CPU GEMM kernels from llamafile; 1.3-5x faster LLM prompt eval than March-2024 llama.cpp, upstreamed since.
what_it_does: llamafile packages llama.cpp and a model into one Cosmopolitan Libc executable. The catalogued part is tinyBLAS, its CPU matrix-multiply kernels for the contiguous case C = A^T * B on F32, F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q4_0 (plus Q5_0/IQ4_NL upstream) weights. The entry point is llamafile_sgemm(params, m, n, k, A, lda, B, ldb, C, ldc, Atype, Btype, Ctype), which returns false when it cannot handle a shape or type so ggml falls back to its own path. It is not a BLAS API replacement.
how_it_is_fast: It unrolls both outer loops of the matmul into a fixed RM x RN tile of accumulator registers (outer-product register tiling, e.g. mnpack<4,6> with 32 vector registers, <4,3> with 16). Each loaded A vector is reused across several B columns, which cuts loads per FMA. It skips the cache-blocking/packing and malloc that MKL-style BLAS does, so it wins on cache-resident matrices. Threads take tile jobs from ggml's own threadpool and barrier, avoiding a second BLAS thread pool, and llamafile picks per-microarchitecture builds at runtime (AVX2, AVX-512F, Zen 4 AVX-512 BF16/VNNI, NEON).
when_to_use: CPU-only LLM inference where prompt processing (prefill, batch n>1) dominates: long prompts, RAG, summarization, LLaVA image tokens.
F16/BF16/F32 weights on x86 with AVX2 or AVX-512, where the blog shows the largest gains (e.g. i9-14900K Mistral 7B f16 50 vs 13 prompt tok/s; 7995WX 485 vs 197).
Small to mid GEMMs that fit in L2 (author's best case: under ~1000 prompt tokens, 512-wide matrices) where MKL's packing overhead dominates.
Shipping one binary that runs on many OSes and CPUs: llamafile dispatches the right kernel at runtime.
Borrowing a compact, MIT-licensed register-tiled GEMM micro-kernel design for your own C++ code (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp in llama.cpp).
when_not_to_use: Token generation (n=1 matvec): memory-bound, and the tables show eval tok/s unchanged (e.g. 17 vs 16 on 7995WX).
Large GEMMs: the author says that at 1024 'MKL wins once more'; use MKL/OpenBLAS/BLIS for general dense linear algebra.
Apple Silicon: off by default on M2 in the upstream PR; on M2 Ultra TinyLlama q8_0 it was slower (457 vs 564 prompt tok/s).
K-quants and other formats outside its supported set: the kernel returns false and you get the regular ggml path.
If you already run a current llama.cpp: the kernels were merged there (default on), so the 2024 speedup is no longer an advantage over upstream.

integration.form: source-drop (one sgemm.cpp/sgemm.h inside ggml), or the whole llamafile executable
integration.dependencies: ggml internals (ggml_compute_params, threadpool, quant block types); llamafile builds also need Cosmopolitan Libc
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (if constexpr); GCC or Clang with target intrinsics; the blog's example used -O3 -ffast-math -march=native; Clang takes about 45 s to compile the kernels (PR #6414)
integration.platforms: x86-64 (AVX/AVX2/AVX-512F/AVX512-BF16), aarch64 NEON (fp16 arithmetic optional); upstream also has POWER (MMA/VSX), s390x VXE and RISC-V RVV variants
integration.thread_safety: Meant to be called by every ggml worker thread with its ith/nth; it coordinates through ggml barriers, so it is not a standalone thread-safe API
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — transparent inside llama.cpp/ggml (GGML_USE_LLAMAFILE, default on), but not a BLAS (sgemm/cblas) interface for other code

gotchas: Silent fallback: it handles only shapes where k is a multiple of the vector width and m a multiple of 4 (n >= 2 except on POWER MMA), and only an F32 output; otherwise it returns false and the slower generic path runs.
No bound on rounding error: the source says error 'grows along with k', and the blog warns ARMv8.2 fp16 accumulation without Kahan summation adds error.
The repo now lives at github.com/mozilla-ai/llamafile; v0.10 rebuilt on a newer llama.cpp and dropped some features (pledge sandbox, localscore, stable diffusion).
LLAMAFILE_DISABLE_SGEMM=1 turns the kernels off in llamafile; use it when you A/B test.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose tinyBLAS for F16/BF16/Q8_0 prefill on x86 or ARM inside a ggml-based stack. Choose T-MAC for 2-4-bit weights or BitNet decoding, and the AVX512 DGEMM tutorial kernels or MKL for double-precision or large general GEMMs.
verified_claims_summary: The author's blog (justine.lol/matmul, March 2024) compares llamafile 0.7 to llama.cpp builds from 2024-03-26/29 on an i9-9900, i9-14900K, Raspberry Pi 4/5, M2 Ultra and Threadripper 7995WX. Prompt tok/s improved by up to 3.8x (14900K f16) and 2.5x (7995WX f16), and by about 1.1-1.6x on Q8_0, while generation tok/s was flat. A single 513x512x512 GEMM on the i9-14900K hit 810 vs MKL's 295 GFLOPS. PR #6414 reports about 2x on F16 and 40% on Q4_0/Q8_0. Flags for the tok/s runs are not stated; first-party only.
status_note: Active (Mozilla.ai, 26.1k stars, commits in Sept 2026); llamafile is Apache-2.0, but the kernels are MIT and already live in llama.cpp, so copy them from there.
